### What does this PR do?

Adds the MXFP4 recipe from the low-precision roadmap (#8186): the MXFP4 counterpart of the MXFP8 recipe in #8127, for the routed experts of MoE models.

- `examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh`: GRPO on Qwen3-30B-A3B with DAPO-Math-17k on one 4-GPU Blackwell node (tested on 4×B300; 4×B200 untested). It uses the data, hyper-parameters and layout of `examples/mxfp8/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh` (training TP2 × EP2, full recompute, optimizer on the CPU; rollout vLLM TP2). `PRECISION` selects the arm:
  - `mxfp4_qat`: MXFP4 rollout experts (`rollout.quantization.moe=MXFP4`) and ModelOpt MXFP4 QAT on the routed experts (`qat.mode=mxfp4`)
  - `mxfp4`: MXFP4 rollout experts only
  - `bf16`: the baseline
- `docs/low_precision/mxfp4.md`: requirements, configuration, notes and the example; linked from `docs/index.rst`.
- The example sets `data.seed` (default 1), so every arm sees the same data order.

Results, ten GRPO steps per arm on one 4×B300 machine (details in the doc page and under Test): QAT cuts the rollout–trainer mismatch of the MXFP4 rollout by 78% (`rollout_corr/kl` 0.0142 → 0.0031; BF16 0.0017) and makes a step 16% longer than the MXFP4 rollout alone (mean step time 1031 s vs 890 s; BF16 829 s).

Depends on #8425: the measured QAT cost and the doc's note on it assume all expert weights of a grouped linear are fake-quantized in one call. Please merge this after #8425.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: no open PR adds an MXFP4 recipe or example (searched `mxfp4`; #7895 is DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert QAT, #8398 the Hopper MoE backend default).
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

```bash
python3 tests/special_sanity/check_docs_time_info.py            # ✅
python3 tests/special_sanity/check_example_naming.py --root examples   # ✅ 112 scripts
python3 tests/special_sanity/check_uv_gpu_only.py               # ✅
python3 tests/special_sanity/validate_structure.py              # ✅
```

All three arms of the new script compose (`--cfg job`, `VERL_USE_UV=0`): the QAT arm resolves to `qat.enable=true`, `qat.mode=mxfp4`, `rollout.quantization.moe=MXFP4`, TP2 × EP2 for actor and ref.

GPU, B300 (SM103), the versions verl locks (vLLM 0.32.0, Transformer Engine 2.16.1, Megatron-Bridge 0.6.2, ModelOpt 0.44.0; the same lock at both verl commits below):

1. verl main 174888fc, one GPU, `scripts/rollout_logprob_diff.py --r3-router-replay` on a small random Qwen3-MoE (4 layers, 32 experts, top-4):

   | Arm | vLLM MoE backend | k3 KL |
   |---|---|---|
   | BF16 | FlashInfer TRT-LLM (unquantized) | 1.0e-5 |
   | MXFP4 rollout experts | `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` | 1.0e-3 |
   | MXFP4 rollout experts + MXFP4 QAT | `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` | 4.0e-5 |

   QAT brings the training forward 26× closer to the MXFP4 rollout.

2. verl main 174888fc, four GPUs, the configuration of this script with `PRECISION=mxfp4_qat` (host-specific cache paths added), one GRPO step on Qwen3-30B-A3B (TP2 × EP2): QAT builds on the Transformer Engine spec with tensor and expert parallelism combined (723 quantizers per rank). Weight sync and the step complete with `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0030. Step time 3743 s: generation 119 s, `old_log_prob` 1015 s, `ref` 105 s, `update_actor` 2423 s, `update_weights` 43 s. The QAT forward (`old_log_prob`) took about 10× the reference forward of the same model (`ref`). Nearly all of it came from ModelOpt fake-quantizing the grouped experts' weights one expert at a time at every forward; with #8425 on main 2ab35292 (the commits in between change the rollout's request gate, DeepSeek-V4 and ROCm guards and tracing, not the training path), the same first step took 1056 s on the same GPUs (`old_log_prob` 179 s, `update_actor` 569 s).

+# MXFP4 MoE RL on Blackwell
+
+Last updated: 10/29/2026
+
+MXFP4 is the OCP microscaling FP4 format: E2M1 elements with one E8M0 scale per 32-element block. In verl it covers
+the routed experts of MoE models. The rollout serves MXFP4 expert weights, quantized on the trainer side, and
+DeepGEMM quantizes the expert activations to FP8 at run time. Training stays in BF16; with QAT, ModelOpt
+fake-quantizes the routed experts during training: their weights exactly as the exported rollout weights, their
+inputs to MXFP8, close to the rollout's FP8 activations.
+
+The rollout quantization interface shared by all formats, the kernel defaults and the format details are described
+in [Low-Precision Rollout and Quantization-Aware Training](qat.md). For MXFP8 end to end, see
+[MXFP8 RL on Blackwell](mxfp8.md).
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Blackwell GPUs for the rollout: the MXFP4-weight × FP8-activation experts are served by vLLM's DeepGEMM FP4 MoE
+  kernel (SM100/SM120). Hopper has no such kernel and is outside this recipe; see [qat.md](qat.md).
+- Training: the Megatron-Bridge model path; QAT uses NVIDIA ModelOpt.
+- Rollout: vLLM (the version verl locks).
+
+## Configuration
+
+```yaml
+# MXFP4 rollout experts; dense layers stay in BF16
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization:
+  linear: null
+  moe: MXFP4
+
+# optional: MXFP4 QAT on the routed experts
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.qat:
+  enable: True
+  mode: mxfp4        # mxfp4_mxfp8 also trains the dense layers with MXFP8 QAT (vLLM: linear: MXFP8)
+```
+
+Notes:
+
+- `lm_head`, the token embedding, MoE routers and every dense layer stay in BF16 on the rollout and in training.
+- During QAT, the routed experts' weights are fake-quantized with the same QDQ as the trainer-side exporter, so the
+  QAT forward and the exported rollout weights agree bit for bit. The experts' inputs are fake-quantized to MXFP8
+  (1x32 blocks), while the rollout's DeepGEMM kernel quantizes them to FP8 in 1x128 groups with E8M0 scales.
+- QAT quantizes the Transformer Engine modules of the layer spec that Megatron-Bridge builds for the model, the
+  grouped expert linears included, so tensor and expert parallelism can be combined.
+- QAT and Transformer Engine FP8 training are mutually exclusive; the engine refuses the combination.
+- QAT fake-quantizes all expert weights of a grouped linear in one call. On the example below, QAT makes a step about
+  16% longer than the MXFP4 rollout alone; with ModelOpt's per-expert loop, the first QAT step took 3743 s instead
+  of 1056 s on the same GPUs.
+
+## Example: Qwen3-30B-A3B on DAPO-Math-17k
+

+# MXFP4 MoE RL on Blackwell
+
+Last updated: 10/29/2026
+
+MXFP4 is the OCP microscaling FP4 format: E2M1 elements with one E8M0 scale per 32-element block. In verl it covers
+the routed experts of MoE models. The rollout serves MXFP4 expert weights, quantized on the trainer side, and
+DeepGEMM quantizes the expert activations to FP8 at run time. Training stays in BF16; with QAT, ModelOpt
+fake-quantizes the routed experts during training: their weights exactly as the exported rollout weights, their
+inputs to MXFP8, close to the rollout's FP8 activations.
+
+The rollout quantization interface shared by all formats, the kernel defaults and the format details are described
+in [Low-Precision Rollout and Quantization-Aware Training](qat.md). For MXFP8 end to end, see
+[MXFP8 RL on Blackwell](mxfp8.md).
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Blackwell GPUs for the rollout: the MXFP4-weight × FP8-activation experts are served by vLLM's DeepGEMM FP4 MoE
+  kernel (SM100/SM120). Hopper has no such kernel and is outside this recipe; see [qat.md](qat.md).
+- Training: the Megatron-Bridge model path; QAT uses NVIDIA ModelOpt.
+- Rollout: vLLM (the version verl locks).
+
+## Configuration
+
+```yaml
+# MXFP4 rollout experts; dense layers stay in BF16
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization:
+  linear: null
+  moe: MXFP4
+
+# optional: MXFP4 QAT on the routed experts
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.qat:
+  enable: True
+  mode: mxfp4        # mxfp4_mxfp8 also trains the dense layers with MXFP8 QAT (vLLM: linear: MXFP8)
+```
+
+Notes:
+
+- `lm_head`, the token embedding, MoE routers and every dense layer stay in BF16 on the rollout and in training.
+- During QAT, the routed experts' weights are fake-quantized with the same QDQ as the trainer-side exporter, so the
+  QAT forward and the exported rollout weights agree bit for bit. The experts' inputs are fake-quantized to MXFP8
+  (1x32 blocks), while the rollout's DeepGEMM kernel quantizes them to FP8 in 1x128 groups with E8M0 scales.
+- QAT quantizes the Transformer Engine modules of the layer spec that Megatron-Bridge builds for the model, the
+  grouped expert linears included, so tensor and expert parallelism can be combined.
+- QAT and Transformer Engine FP8 training are mutually exclusive; the engine refuses the combination.
+- QAT fake-quantizes all expert weights of a grouped linear in one call. On the example below, QAT makes a step about
+  16% longer than the MXFP4 rollout alone; with ModelOpt's per-expert loop, the first QAT step took 3743 s instead
+  of 1056 s on the same GPUs.
+
+## Example: Qwen3-30B-A3B on DAPO-Math-17k
+
+[`examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh)
+is the MXFP4 counterpart of the MXFP8 Qwen3-30B-A3B example, with the same data and hyper-parameters on one
+4-GPU Blackwell node (tested on 4×B300; 4×B200 untested): training TP2 × EP2 with full recompute and the whole
+optimizer on the CPU, the rollout vLLM with TP2. `PRECISION` selects the arm: `mxfp4_qat` (MXFP4 rollout experts and
+MXFP4 QAT), `mxfp4` (MXFP4 rollout experts only) and `bf16` (the baseline). The script reads DAPO-Math-17k in verl's
+format from `TRAIN_FILE`, as
+[verl-recipe's `dapo/prepare_dapo_data.sh`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-recipe/blob/main/dapo/prepare_dapo_data.sh)
+downloads it, and runs without a validation set.
+
+```bash
+PRECISION=mxfp4_qat TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=10 bash examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh
+PRECISION=mxfp4 TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=10 bash examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh
+PRECISION=bf16 TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=10 bash examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh
+```
+
+### Results
+
+**Configuration**
+
+- One 4×B300 machine for every arm, the same seed and data order, so steps pair across arms; 10 steps
+- The script's hyper-parameters, as in the MXFP8 example: 64 prompts × 8 responses per step, prompts and responses up
+  to 1024 and 8192 tokens, dynamic batching at 20,480 tokens per GPU, learning rate 1e-6; DAPO-Math-17k deduplicated
+  to its 17,398 unique prompts

### What does this PR do?

Adds the MXFP4 recipe from the low-precision roadmap (#8186): the MXFP4 counterpart of the MXFP8 recipe in #8127, for the routed experts of MoE models.

- `examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh`: GRPO on Qwen3-30B-A3B with DAPO-Math-17k on one 4-GPU Blackwell node (tested on 4×B300; 4×B200 untested). It uses the data, hyper-parameters and layout of `examples/mxfp8/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh` (training TP2 × EP2, full recompute, optimizer on the CPU; rollout vLLM TP2). `PRECISION` selects the arm:
  - `mxfp4_qat`: MXFP4 rollout experts (`rollout.quantization.moe=MXFP4`) and ModelOpt MXFP4 QAT on the routed experts (`qat.mode=mxfp4`)
  - `mxfp4`: MXFP4 rollout experts only
  - `bf16`: the baseline
- `docs/low_precision/mxfp4.md`: requirements, configuration, notes and the example; linked from `docs/index.rst`.
- The example sets `data.seed` (default 1), so every arm sees the same data order.

Results, ten GRPO steps per arm on one 4×B300 machine (details in the doc page and under Test): QAT cuts the rollout–trainer mismatch of the MXFP4 rollout by 78% (`rollout_corr/kl` 0.0142 → 0.0031; BF16 0.0017) and makes a step 16% longer than the MXFP4 rollout alone (mean step time 1031 s vs 890 s; BF16 829 s).

Depends on #8425: the measured QAT cost and the doc's note on it assume all expert weights of a grouped linear are fake-quantized in one call. Please merge this after #8425.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: no open PR adds an MXFP4 recipe or example (searched `mxfp4`; #7895 is DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert QAT, #8398 the Hopper MoE backend default).
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

```bash
python3 tests/special_sanity/check_docs_time_info.py            # ✅
python3 tests/special_sanity/check_example_naming.py --root examples   # ✅ 112 scripts
python3 tests/special_sanity/check_uv_gpu_only.py               # ✅
python3 tests/special_sanity/validate_structure.py              # ✅
```

All three arms of the new script compose (`--cfg job`, `VERL_USE_UV=0`): the QAT arm resolves to `qat.enable=true`, `qat.mode=mxfp4`, `rollout.quantization.moe=MXFP4`, TP2 × EP2 for actor and ref.

GPU, B300 (SM103), the versions verl locks (vLLM 0.32.0, Transformer Engine 2.16.1, Megatron-Bridge 0.6.2, ModelOpt 0.44.0; the same lock at both verl commits below):

1. verl main 174888fc, one GPU, `scripts/rollout_logprob_diff.py --r3-router-replay` on a small random Qwen3-MoE (4 layers, 32 experts, top-4):

   | Arm | vLLM MoE backend | k3 KL |
   |---|---|---|
   | BF16 | FlashInfer TRT-LLM (unquantized) | 1.0e-5 |
   | MXFP4 rollout experts | `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` | 1.0e-3 |

+# MXFP4 MoE QAT on Blackwell
+
+Last updated: 11/03/2026
+
+MXFP4 is the OCP microscaling FP4 format: E2M1 elements with one E8M0 scale per 32-element block. In verl it covers
+the routed experts of MoE models. The rollout serves MXFP4 expert weights, quantized on the trainer side, and
+DeepGEMM quantizes the expert activations to FP8 at run time. Transformer Engine has no MXFP4 training, so training
+stays in BF16; with QAT, the routed experts are fake-quantized during training: their weights exactly as the
+exported rollout weights, their inputs to MXFP8, close to the rollout's FP8 activations.
+
+The rollout quantization interface shared by all formats, the kernel defaults and the format details are described
+in [Low-Precision Rollout and Quantization-Aware Training](qat.md). For MXFP8 end to end, see
+[MXFP8 RL on Blackwell](mxfp8.md).
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Blackwell GPUs for the rollout: the MXFP4-weight × FP8-activation experts are served by vLLM's DeepGEMM FP4 MoE
+  kernel (SM100/SM120). Hopper has no such kernel and is outside this recipe; see [qat.md](qat.md).
+- Training: the Megatron-Bridge model path; QAT uses NVIDIA ModelOpt.
+- Rollout: vLLM (the version verl locks).
+
+## Configuration
+
+```yaml
+# MXFP4 rollout experts; dense layers stay in BF16
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization:
+  linear: null
+  moe: MXFP4
+
+# optional: MXFP4 QAT on the routed experts
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.qat:
+  enable: True
+  mode: mxfp4        # mxfp4_mxfp8 also trains the dense layers with MXFP8 QAT (vLLM: linear: MXFP8)
+```
+
+Notes:
+
+- `lm_head`, the token embedding, MoE routers and every dense layer stay in BF16 on the rollout and in training.
+- ModelOpt installs the fake quantizers; they run verl's TileLang MXFP4 kernel, the one the trainer-side exporter
+  uses without dequantization, so the QAT forward and the exported rollout weights agree bit for bit (see
+  [qat.md](qat.md)). The experts' inputs are fake-quantized to MXFP8 (1x32 blocks), while the rollout's DeepGEMM
+  kernel quantizes them to FP8 in 1x128 groups with E8M0 scales.
+- QAT quantizes the Transformer Engine modules of the layer spec that Megatron-Bridge builds for the model, the
+  grouped expert linears included, so tensor and expert parallelism can be combined. All expert weights of a grouped
+  linear are fake-quantized in one kernel launch.
+- QAT and Transformer Engine FP8 training are mutually exclusive; the engine refuses the combination.
+
+## Example: Qwen3-30B-A3B on DAPO-Math-17k
+
+[`examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh)
+is the MXFP4 counterpart of the MXFP8 Qwen3-30B-A3B example, with the same data and hyper-parameters on one
+4-GPU Blackwell node (tested on 4×B300; 4×B200 untested): training TP2 × EP2 with full recompute and the whole
+optimizer on the CPU, the rollout vLLM with TP2. `PRECISION` selects the arm: `mxfp4_qat` (MXFP4 rollout experts and
+MXFP4 QAT), `mxfp4` (MXFP4 rollout experts only) and `bf16` (the baseline). The script reads DAPO-Math-17k in verl's
+format from `TRAIN_FILE`, as
+[verl-recipe's `dapo/prepare_dapo_data.sh`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-recipe/blob/main/dapo/prepare_dapo_data.sh)
+downloads it, and runs without a validation set.
+
+```bash
+PRECISION=mxfp4_qat TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=10 bash examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh
+PRECISION=mxfp4 TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=10 bash examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh
+PRECISION=bf16 TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=10 bash examples/mxfp4/run_qwen3_30b_a3b_megatron.sh
+```
+
+### Results
+
+> These runs predate verl's TileLang QAT and export kernels and ModelOpt 0.47 (verl main 2ab35292, with the expert
+> weights of a grouped linear stacked and fake-quantized in one call); they are being rerun on current main.
+
+**Configuration**
+
+- One 4×B300 machine for every arm, the same seed and data order, so steps pair across arms; 10 steps
+- The script's hyper-parameters, as in the MXFP8 example: 64 prompts × 8 responses per step, prompts and responses up
+  to 1024 and 8192 tokens, dynamic batching at 20,480 tokens per GPU, learning rate 1e-6; DAPO-Math-17k deduplicated
+  to its 17,398 unique prompts
+- The versions verl locks: vLLM 0.32.0, Transformer Engine 2.16.1, Megatron-Core 0.19.2, ModelOpt 0.44.0
+
+"X/Y" is training precision X, rollout precision Y; BF16+QAT trains in BF16 with MXFP4 QAT on the routed experts.
+
+| mean of steps 1–10 | BF16/BF16 | BF16/MXFP4 | BF16+QAT/MXFP4 |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| step time (s) | 829 | 890 | 1031 |
+| generation (s) | 107 | 113 | 113 |
+| `old_log_prob` (s) | 118 | 126 | 166 |
+| `update_actor` (s) | 475 | 478 | 576 |
+| `update_weights` (s) | 7 | 45 | 46 |
+| `rollout_corr/kl` | 0.0017 | 0.0142 | 0.0031 |
+| score | −0.191 | −0.157 | −0.156 |
+
+Results and observations:
+
+- QAT cuts the rollout–trainer mismatch of the MXFP4 rollout by 78%, to 1.8× the BF16 arm's. Per step,
+  `rollout_corr/kl` ranged 0.0027–0.0036 with QAT, 0.0127–0.0164 without it and 0.0016–0.0019 in BF16.
+- QAT makes a step 16% longer than the MXFP4 rollout alone: `old_log_prob` +40 s, `update_actor` +97 s.
+- The MXFP4 rollout does not speed this job up: generation takes about as long as in BF16, and exporting the MXFP4
+  expert weights adds about 38 s per step to `update_weights`.
+- Ten steps are enough for speed and mismatch, not for the score.

+Last updated: 10/29/2026
+
+MXFP4 is the OCP microscaling FP4 format: E2M1 elements with one E8M0 scale per 32-element block. In verl it covers
+the routed experts of MoE models. The rollout serves MXFP4 expert weights, quantized on the trainer side, and
+DeepGEMM quantizes the expert activations to FP8 at run time. Training stays in BF16; with QAT, ModelOpt
+fake-quantizes the routed experts during training: their weights exactly as the exported rollout weights, their
+inputs to MXFP8, close to the rollout's FP8 activations.
+
+The rollout quantization interface shared by all formats, the kernel defaults and the format details are described
+in [Low-Precision Rollout and Quantization-Aware Training](qat.md). For MXFP8 end to end, see
+[MXFP8 RL on Blackwell](mxfp8.md).
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Blackwell GPUs for the rollout: the MXFP4-weight × FP8-activation experts are served by vLLM's DeepGEMM FP4 MoE
+  kernel (SM100/SM120). Hopper has no such kernel and is outside this recipe; see [qat.md](qat.md).
+- Training: the Megatron-Bridge model path; QAT uses NVIDIA ModelOpt.
+- Rollout: vLLM (the version verl locks).
+
+## Configuration
+
+```yaml
+# MXFP4 rollout experts; dense layers stay in BF16
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization:
+  linear: null
+  moe: MXFP4
+
+# optional: MXFP4 QAT on the routed experts
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.qat:
+  enable: True
+  mode: mxfp4        # mxfp4_mxfp8 also trains the dense layers with MXFP8 QAT (vLLM: linear: MXFP8)
+```
+
+Notes:
+
+- `lm_head`, the token embedding, MoE routers and every dense layer stay in BF16 on the rollout and in training.
+- During QAT, the routed experts' weights are fake-quantized with the same QDQ as the trainer-side exporter, so the
+  QAT forward and the exported rollout weights agree bit for bit. The experts' inputs are fake-quantized to MXFP8
+  (1x32 blocks), while the rollout's DeepGEMM kernel quantizes them to FP8 in 1x128 groups with E8M0 scales.
+- QAT quantizes the Transformer Engine modules of the layer spec that Megatron-Bridge builds for the model, the
+  grouped expert linears included, so tensor and expert parallelism can be combined.
+- QAT and Transformer Engine FP8 training are mutually exclusive; the engine refuses the combination.
+- QAT fake-quantizes all expert weights of a grouped linear in one call. On the example below, QAT makes a step about
+  16% longer than the MXFP4 rollout alone; with ModelOpt's per-expert loop, the first QAT step took 3743 s instead
+  of 1056 s on the same GPUs.

+optimizer on the CPU, the rollout vLLM with TP2. `PRECISION` selects the arm: `mxfp4_qat` (MXFP4 rollout experts and
+MXFP4 QAT), `mxfp4` (MXFP4 rollout experts only) and `bf16` (the baseline). The script reads DAPO-Math-17k in verl's

+# GRPO | Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE) | DAPO-Math-17k | Megatron training | MXFP4 routed experts | NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100+)

+
+set -xeuo pipefail

+
+########################### user-adjustable ###########################

+

+TRAIN_FILE=${TRAIN_FILE:-$HOME/data/dapo-math-17k/train.parquet}
+# only read when TEST_FREQ > 0
